text:
incident-bot: Pager: High-severity — multi-GPU communicator errors in tp4-pool-17 (NCCL timeouts). Hits: 12 active jobs, first seen 03:04:52 UTC. Escalation: oncall dave_oncall. :rotating_light:

Dave_oncall: on it, joining bridge. Can someone grab the most recent logs and which customer jobs are impacted?

alice_sre: seeing repeated `NCCL WARN` and then `SIGTERM` in the container logs. Suspect kube OOM or preemption. Pasting tail: 

--- logs ---
[2026-03-15T03:03:49Z] worker-3 | NCCL WARN NET/UNEXP 0x3e8
[2026-03-15T03:03:50Z] worker-3 | NCCL INFO Comm 2 error: Unrecoverable (timeout)
[2026-03-15T03:03:51Z] worker-3 | terminating process due to signal 15 (SIGTERM)
--- end ---

ben_runtime: getting `SIGTERM` inside container usually means kubelet killed the pod. checking kube events now.

carla_ml: which models were running? any pipeline-parallel shards?

alice_sre: yes, several tp4 tensor/pipeline parallel jobs. Model: open-psi-v2 (sharded across 4 GPUs).

ben_runtime: `kubectl -n ml get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=pod/tp4-job-47` shows repeated `Killing` due to `preemption` at 03:03:51. Node reported `kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (python)`.

-- snippet --
Mar 15 03:03:50 node-17 kernel: [123456.789] Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (python) total-vm:5260000kB, anon-rss:4700000kB
-- end --

eve_support: customer-facing: frank_customer reported increased 504s and a spike in request latency for their endpoint. He says about ~5% error rate for last 10m.

frank_customer: yep, saw a bunch of timeouts. We have jobs pinned to tp4; can you confirm if any inference was lost or rerouted?

Dave_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-17, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) scale up fallback capacity (tp4-burst) and update routing to use lower-shard variant (open-psi-v2-2g) while we recover. Ben/Alice to execute.

ben_runtime: cordoning node-17 now: `kubectl cordon node-17` — done. Draining non-prod pods, but need to `--ignore-daemonsets` for monitoring.

alice_sre: starting controlled drain of ML pods; will use `kubectl drain node-17 --delete-local-data --force --ignore-daemonsets` but will keep one model shard up if possible for graceful handoff.

deploy-bot: Autoscaler triggered +2 nodes in tp4-burst at 03:05:10 UTC (req by policy).

carla_ml: switching routing table to fallback model variant: `route set open-psi-v2 -> open-psi-v2-2g` with 100% for customer frank-corp for now. Doing a canary to 25% first.

Dave_oncall: good. Monitor latency and errorrate. Eve, keep frank_customer updated.

eve_support: @frank_customer we've routed a fallback variant and scaled capacity. Expect lower QPS for a few minutes while warmup happens. Will update in 5 min. :thumbsup:

frank_customer: thanks. key concern is correctness of responses — we'll run quick smoke tests on a small sample.

alice_sre: more logs: seeing `CUDA: GPU 1 Xid 79: GPU memory access fault` right before OOM in some pods. Could be memory leak or model memory spike due to batch sizing.

ben_runtime: checking node metrics — memory pressure peaked at 98% across GPUs; one pod had a runaway allocation: `python -c 'torch.empty(1e9).cuda()'` style oom trace in the stack. Might be a client job misbehaving.

carla_ml: we should add a per-pod GPU memory limit/preempt policy to guard against runaway jobs. But short term, are we ok with draining node-17 and letting autoscaler bring replacement nodes?

Dave_oncall: yes. alice, confirm drain progress. ben, ensure scheduler doesn't pack more shards onto single nodes while cluster stabilizes.

alice_sre: drain done for non-critical pods. Two critical model shards were evicted; the controller restarted them on node-19 and node-20. However, NCCL communicator couldn't reestablish for tp4-job-47 — I see `ncclCommInitAll` failing with `unreachable peer`.

-- nccl snippet --
E ncclCommInitRank failed, ret=2, reason=unreachable peer
stack: at /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/parallel...
-- end --

ben_runtime: forced restart of the job's controller pod to pick up rebalanced assignments. Restarting now.

Dave_oncall: while we wait for restarts, create incident bridge summary and page eng-runtime. This smells like two simultaneous issues: node OOM + NCCL reinitialization fragility on partial shard moves.

ben_runtime: eng-runtime pinged. @ben_runtime -> @alice_sre: attaching kube logs and dmesg.

-- kube logs snippet --
kubectl logs pod/tp4-job-47-controller -n ml --tail=200\[...]
2026-03-15T03:04:12Z controller | reassigning shard 2 -> node-20
2026-03-15T03:04:21Z controller | launch worker pods: tp4-job-47-worker-2
2026-03-15T03:04:33Z worker-2 | NCCL INFO starting comm init
2026-03-15T03:04:36Z worker-2 | NCCL INFO comm init success (partial)
2026-03-15T03:04:48Z worker-1 | NCCL WARN timeout waiting for barrier
2026-03-15T03:04:52Z worker-2 | SIGTERM received, terminating
-- end --

carla_ml: our eval harness shows fallback variant preserves 98.7% token-level parity on small test set — acceptable as short-term.

frank_customer: thanks for the quick switch. We'll keep running smoke tests and will report anomalies.

alice_sre: additional note: node-17 had a recent kernel CVE backport applied in last night's maintenance window. Correlating with kernel oom behaviour — opening a ticket with infra for kernel tuning rollback.

ben_runtime: after the restart, the job recovered slowly — 3/4 shards rejoined, one remained stuck with `ncclCommConnect timeout`. Manual restart of that worker pod fixed it. Marking as mitigation step: restart stuck worker pods when communicator init fails for >60s.

Dave_oncall: mitigation timeline: 03:03:49 alert -> 03:05:10 autoscale -> 03:06:00 routing fallback -> 03:10:12 most jobs recovered; frank-corp saw transient 504s ~5% for ~7m.

eve_support: logged customer impact: frank-corp, frank-corp-internal (svc ids 9876, 9877). Notified account team.

carla_ml: action items (short):
- pin temporary routing to fallback for frank-corp and related tenants (carla)
- enable per-pod GPU memory guard on tp4 (alice + ben)
- autoscaler policy review to avoid packing shards (ben)
- infra: investigate kernel memory behaviour on node-17 (alice -> infra)
- eng-runtime: improve NCCL reinit robustness and add backoff on shard moves (ben -> eng-runtime)

Dave_oncall: creating incident (INC-2026-0315-03) and assigning P0. Postmortem owner: ben_runtime. Please add timelines and logs.

deploy-bot: Created INC-2026-0315-03 and linked this thread.

frank_customer: appreciate the updates. Keep us posted on postmortem.

alice_sre: final note before wrap: adding a short-term guard: kill pods that exceed 95% GPU memory for >30s to avoid OOM cascade. Will ship as a cluster admission webhook test.

Dave_oncall: wrap up: monitor for 1h, if no regressions mark Incident Resolved. Thanks all. :heart:

incident-bot: Incident severity -> P0 Escalated. Bridge closed at 03:28:30 UTC (follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-0315-03).
